correctness.rationale: The cyclic sine stationary equations are exhausted by the 0/pi cases and k=0,3 triple-angle solutions; for positive t!=1 these give exactly 8 or 12 points. The constrained cosine Hessian has nonzero determinant at all eight Boolean points and at each of the four new points, with indices (1,3,3,1)/(1,5,5,1). The exact weighted-Laplacian spectrum yields smooth descent for all 0<h<2/Lambda. Finite critical points plus vanishing gradient imply each orbit has a singleton omega limit. Analytic nonzero Jacobian determinant implies null-preimages of the stable manifolds of hyperbolic saddles, even when the map is not globally invertible. Antiphase local multipliers establish sharpness. Verification file independently samples 1852 finite diagnostics; it does not prove the infinite result. Strict descent rules out noncritical winding fixed points in the stated step interval; no statement is made beyond it.

value.rationale: A natural infinitesimal detuning resolves the non-Morse critical circles of the repulsive square in two fundamentally distinct ways, with a sharp 8/12 actual critical-point jump, full index distribution and explicit new saddles. The analytic-null-preimage argument extends almost-global attraction through potentially noninvertible Euler steps all the way to the optimal local linear threshold. This refines the known generic complex count and general descent estimates with a structurally motivated exact bifurcation classification.
